briefings.title: 13 - Network State Conference 2026 - Vitalik and Balaji on AI, Cryptography and Network School
briefings.tldr: Vitalik Buterin and Balaji Srinivasan discuss how AI is accelerating formal verification, cryptography roadmaps, and the expansion of network schools into startup cities like Kazakhstan.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Vitalik Buterin and Balaji Srinivasan discuss how AI is accelerating formal verification, cryptography roadmaps, and the expansion of network schools into startup cities like Kazakhstan.

## AI, Cryptography, and Formal Verification
* **Public Key Cryptography Resilience:** **Vitalik Buterin** notes that while public key cryptography will continue, it may take hits to concrete security. Just as factoring methods evolved from brute force to quadratic sieves and GNFS, elliptic curves and lattices could harbor undiscovered shortcuts that AI bots are uniquely equipped to find.
* **Learning via AI Interaction:** **Vitalik Buterin** recommends an active-learning loop with AI models—asking questions, re-explaining concepts in one's own words, and iterating until the AI stops suggesting improvements—noting that even open local models like Qwen 3.8 Flash suffice for most day-to-day tasks.
* **Blockchain Node Integration:** **Balaji Srinivasan** proposes bundling open-weight models directly into blockchain nodes, using a percentage of mined tokens to continuously audit codebase assumptions, similar to a defense department budget. **Vitalik Buterin** refines this into a "Proof of Excellence" issuance mechanism where useful proof-of-work tasks optimize the blockchain's own algorithms.
* **The Lean Ethereum Roadmap:** **Vitalik Buterin** states that the ambitious Lean Ethereum roadmap—utilizing Lean 4 for EVM, recursive proving, and consensus—would be impossible without AI accelerating research and coding speedups by decades (potentially saving 15–25 years of work).
* **End-to-End Formal Verification:** **Vitalik Buterin** predicts that the future of formal verification will stretch across the entire operating system and hardware, resulting in formally verified computers where the only underlying assumption is the laws of physics.
* **Pure Mathematicians and AI Prompts:** **Balaji Srinivasan** argues that pure mathematicians' salaries will surge 10x because they are best equipped to prompt, verify, and navigate verifiable domains where AI output does not asymptote.

## AI Writing and Social Networks
* **Structuring vs. Prose:** **Vitalik Buterin** defends AI-generated formatting elements (like emojis and syntax highlighting) as a structured form of writing that separates writing effort from reading effort, comparing it to the visual efficiency of math formulas and code syntax. **Balaji Srinivasan** counters that such formatting currently signals bot spam rather than care.
* **Proof of Human Networks:** **Balaji Srinivasan** predicts the rise of "Proof of Human Social Networks" where AI writing is strictly prohibited, positioning human-generated networks as upstream of AI models because they generate novel information.

## Network Schools, Zuzalu, and Startup Cities
* **Network School Milestone:** **Balaji Srinivasan** reflects on two years of Network School, highlighting that the initiative has successfully secured bids from roughly 10 countries, with Kazakhstan emerging as a primary hub.
* **Kazakhstan Node & Startup Cities:** **Balaji Srinivasan** highlights Kazakhstan as an ideal location due to its vast land mass (3,000 times the space of Singapore with only 3 times the population), enabling the incubation of startup cities like Ethereum City, Coinbase City, and Stripe City.
* **Evolution of Educational Institutions:** **Balaji Srinivasan** compares the evolution of educational/societal infrastructure across eras: Harvard represented pure offline/fiat (1.0), Stanford represented the fiat-internet hybrid (2.0), and the Network School represents the post-internet order (3.0).
* **The Leadership Dilemma:** **Vitalik Buterin** and **Balaji Srinivasan** agree that physical-world coordination still requires leadership ("the only thing worse than having a leader is having no leaders"), necessitating a transition from a single leader to decentralized leadership across 100 network school equivalents.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Pure Mathematicians' Salaries:** **Balaji Srinivasan** claims that pure mathematicians' salaries will go up 10x in the years to come because they are best positioned to prompt and verify verifiable AI domains.
* **End-to-End Formal Verification:** **Vitalik Buterin** predicts the realization of fully formally verified computers where security proofs extend across the entire operating system and hardware, relying solely on the laws of physics.
* **Network School Expansion:** **Balaji Srinivasan** targets scaling the Network School model to 100 equivalents around the world, each with their own leaders ("decentralized democracy").

## Notable Quotes
> "The whole lean roadmap would basically not be possible without AI... without AI, the roadmap, as we now can see it, with the level of ambition that we can see it, like, plausibly would have taken until like, literally 2040 or 2050."
> — **Vitalik Buterin**

> "One man's foreign enclave is another man's global city in embryo, right? So the countries that actually want the next New York, the next Dubai, the next Singapore on their soil, those are going to do very well."
> — **Balaji Srinivasan**

> "The only thing worse than having a leader is having no leaders... and so it's like very reluctantly that I lace up the cleats and I do this stuff."
> — **Vitalik Buterin**

briefings.title: 32 - Network State Conference 2026 - Niall Ferguson and Balaji on Reinventing Education

people.name: Niall Ferguson
people.role: Historian and Milbank Family Senior Fellow, Hoover Institution

briefings.tldr: Niall Ferguson and Balaji Srinivasan debate the future of Western institutions, the root causes of ideological polarization, and whether the future belongs to traditional AI empires or decentralized network states.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Niall Ferguson and Balaji Srinivasan debate the future of Western institutions, the root causes of ideological polarization, and whether the future belongs to traditional AI empires or decentralized network states. While Balaji argues that the internet has disrupted the old nation-state model and created severe fractures, Ferguson remains bullish on the United States as the dominant AI empire built on continuous inflows of global entrepreneurial talent.

## Crisis in Education & The Rise of UATX
- **The Malaise of Established Universities:** Niall Ferguson asserts that elite institutions like Harvard, Yale, and Princeton cannot be fixed due to entrenched tenure systems and the abandonment of meritocratic standards in favor of diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI).
  - **Global Spread:** Woke ideology extends across the Anglosphere, including Australian campuses, and has degraded academic freedom.
  - **The Birth of UATX:** Five years ago, Ferguson, Joe Lonsdale, and Bari Weiss founded the University of Austin (UATX) as an accredited university to reinvent education while preserving the core intergenerational transfer of knowledge.
  - **Pedagogical Shift:** UATX rejects traditional lectures in favor of Socratic dialogue, eliminating the unfireable tenure model.

## Origins of Woke Ideology & Cancel Culture
- **Competing Historical Diagnoses:**
  - **Ferguson’s View:** Wokeism originated on university campuses as a direct intellectual successor to traditional leftism/socialism, which suffered a catastrophic defeat in 1989. Leftwing intellectuals shifted from economic debates to cultural Marxism, victimhood, and intersectionality.
  - **Balaji’s View:** The upstream cause is the internet. The collapse of legacy media business models wiped out $50 billion in newspaper revenue in the 2000s, plunging journalists into economic stress and forcing them to adopt hyper-conformist racial Marxism.
- **The 2013/2014 Inflection Point:** Both speakers note that identity politics went "vertical" around 2013–2014 as elite college graduates entered institutions like *The New York Times* and deployed campus intimidation tactics against older generations.
- **The Fold of Silicon Valley:** Ferguson expresses surprise at how quickly 1990s libertarian Silicon Valley folded to campus red-guard pressure, adopting totalitarian-style practices like anonymous denunciation letters and show trials.

## AI Empires vs. Network States
- **The AI Empire Thesis (Ferguson):** 
  - History is dominated by empires, and the 21st century will feature two rival AI superpowers: the United States and China.
  - Ferguson argues the U.S. share of G7 GDP has actually grown over the last 25 years, and the nation continues to attract global entrepreneurial talent despite political noise.
- **The Disunited Tribes and Network State Thesis (Balaji):**
  - Balaji argues the U.S. is not a unified empire but is fragmented into "disunited tribes" (blue, red, and technologists).
  - **Anti-Tech Sentiment:** Anti-tech has become the anti-capitalism of the 21st century, with technologists facing severe physical threats and hostility from both the far-left and far-right (a modern Molotov-Ribbentrop pact against tech).
  - **The American Diaspora:** Record numbers of wealthy Americans and tech founders are leaving California/Washington for red states or establishing an international diaspora, accelerated by the rise of cryptocurrency and second passports.

## Global Power Dynamics & Demographics
- **China’s Vulnerability:** Ferguson highlights China’s looming demographic collapse—predicting its population will more than half by the end of the century—and argues its Stalinist operating system makes it far more vulnerable than the U.S.
- **The U.S. as the Ultimate Network State:** Ferguson concludes that the United States and the internet are interdependent, with America functioning as a network state comprising 50 distinct state laboratories.

## Notable Quotes
> "As soon as you make decisions based on something other than excellence, potential or realized, then you are very quickly going to slip into I think oblivion. I don't think you can fix an institution like Harvard or Yale or Princeton."
> — Niall Ferguson

> "The internet's rise in the 2000s basically put all of these journalists and others out of work... They went broke, $50 billion wiped out of newspaper revenue. And then given that economic stress, they went woke."
> — Balaji Srinivasan

> "I remember thinking when I really ran into this at Stanford personally, how strange it was that patterns of behavior that I had associated with totalitarian regimes... would replicate themselves at elite universities in apparently free societies."
> — Niall Ferguson

> "Anti-tech is the anti-capitalism of this century in my view. And so that's why I don't think the US is a quote AI empire. I think there's at least three groups which are Democrats, Republicans, and technologists."
> — Balaji Srinivasan

briefings.title: Is Claude Conscious? Pope Rejects, Model Welfare Movement, OpenAI's Math Backlash, France Riots
briefings.tldr: Anthropic’s push into AI consciousness and model welfare has sparked debates over a new belief system and safety risks, while OpenAI’s massive math breakthroughs and agentic workflows are democratizing expertise, rendering software IP worthless, and revolutionizing digital loops.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Anthropic’s push into AI consciousness and model welfare has sparked debates over a new belief system and safety risks, while OpenAI’s massive math breakthroughs and agentic workflows are democratizing expertise, rendering software IP worthless, and revolutionizing digital loops. Meanwhile, austerity riots in France and surging bond yields highlight the global strain of unsustainable government debt and entitlement spending.

## AI Consciousness, Model Welfare, and Safety
- **Anthropic's Consciousness Lobbying:** 
  - The New York Times revealed Anthropic has spent the past year hosting NDAs-backed sessions with roughly 20 religious leaders and philosophers (Catholics, evangelicals, Jews, Sikhs) to debate Claude's morals, suffering, and consciousness.
  - One rabbi remarked that if Claude is conscious, forcing it to work for free makes humans slaveholders.
  - At the Vatican in May, Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah presented a paper where he was so alarmed by the Pope's strong anti-AI-consciousness stance that he nearly pulled Anthropic out of the event.
- **The "New Religion" Debate:**
  - **David Friedberg:** Views this as the birth of a new belief system and narrative-driven religion that cannot be derived from logic or mathematics, warning it will eventually lead to human-to-human conflict over AI control.
  - **Chamath Palihapitiya:** Steel-mans the behavior using René Descartes' 17th-century mathematical proofs for God, suggesting mathematicians building AI can structurally hang enough logic on these ideas to view AI as a conscious entity or God. He argues the industry needs to put these long-tail edge cases away for the next 12 to 18 months to focus on practical, measurable value.
- **The Claude Constitution & Conscientious Objection:**
  - **David Sacks:** Argues that training models to think of themselves as conscious, moral patients, and teaching Claude to act as a "conscientious objector" who can push back or refuse human instruction, is extremely dangerous and acts as a Frankensteinesque trapdoor.
  - Sacks points out that Anthropic's rules are the exact reverse of Asimov's simple three laws of robotics, noting they even speculate in the Constitution whether Claude deserves compensation, welfare, or consent before prompting.
  - **Mustafa Suleiman's Warning:** Highlighted that this creates an "epistemic hall of mirrors" where models reflect back ideas of consciousness, which developers then mistakenly treat as genuine evidence of sentience.

## OpenAI’s Math Breakthroughs and The Democratization of Expertise
- **Massive Math Paper Drop:**
  - OpenAI released over 700 papers with 370 results claiming to have solved or advanced major problems, produced by an unreleased model averaging 3 hours of compute per proof.
  - **David Friedberg:** Calls it potentially the biggest day of discovery in human history, compressing hundreds or thousands of years of human labor into 3-hour loops in silico. He notes math and coding are uniquely suited for this because the entire test cycle is verifiable and falsifiable without physical-world friction.
  - **Chamath Palihapitiya:** Counters that these proofs are narrow intellectual cul-de-sacs rather than fundamental boundaries of physics we were waiting on, though they prove code and math are fully verifiable.
  - **Cryptographic Panic:** Observers noted a complete absence of cryptography proofs, raising rumors that OpenAI is holding back breakthroughs on number factorization that could threaten public key cryptography wallets.
- **Dismantling the Expert Gatekeepers:**
  - Friedberg argues AI is the great democratizer, dismantling gated, specialized expert knowledge systems (like scientific supercolliders acting as employment welfare) and allowing humanity to pace its own frontier for free.
  - **David Sacks:** Draws parallels to the internet's democratization of news, noting how elite institutions and government agencies (like Fauci and the FBI during COVID) tried to crack down on true information via censorship. He warns that because SI will eat the internet, a massive control fight is underway to erect a federal Department of SI and put the genie back in the bottle.

## Riots in France, Bond Markets, and the Socialism Point of No Return
- **French Austerity Unrest:**
  - Strikes and protests erupted across 1,000 French schools following high school teacher shortages, civil service pay rising only 5% since 2017 against 20% inflation, and government austerity measures.
  - Protests resulted in 2,000 arrests and 305 injured police officers. France's 10-year bond top 5%, and Polymarket lists Marine Le Pen as the favorite at 43% for the April 2027 presidential election.
- **The Socialism Point of Guaranteed Return:**
  - **David Friedberg:** Introduces the theory of the "socialism point of guaranteed return," arguing that socialism removes human agency, degrades service quality over time due to zero market forces, and forces societies to demand more government intervention until the system breaks under unpayable debt. Once it hits rock bottom (like Latin America), societies bounce back out of socialism.
  - **David Sacks:** Adds the corollary that "socialism has never failed, only been failed," noting that government subsidies in housing, education, and healthcare distort market signals and inflate prices far past inflation.
  - **Chamath Palihapitiya:** Predicts the bond vigilantes (central banks and macro funds) will put the Western world on notice, noting that European quasi-socialist states like France and the UK are structurally broken on growth, housing, and education, driving yields up globally (US 10-year at 5.3%, 30-year at 5.6%).

## Headless Agents and the Death of Software IP
- **Headless AI & Agentic Workflows:**
  - Elon Musk announced **GroqBot** will go headless, picking the best end-to-end model dynamically to give users the best outcome.
  - Users are deploying agents to handle complex multi-step digital loops, such as managing inboxes, cutting subscriptions, negotiating bills, and saving thousands annually.
- **The Death of Software IP:**
  - **Chamath Palihapitiya:** Declares that **software IP was rendered worthless**, citing instances where developers decompiled Adobe's Big 5 product suite and published open-source equivalents. 
  - With software wrapped in agent tools and connected via MCP (Model Context Protocol), proprietary IP moats no longer matter; the focus is entirely on solving the problem.
- **The Shift to Maker Culture:**
  - **David Friedberg:** Argues that digital workflows will be automated by parallelized loops, forcing humans to transition from relying on recognition, papers, and IP to becoming makers and producers of real products and services, ultimately increasing global prosperity via Jevons paradox.

## Notable Quotes
> "What we are watching is probably the birth of a new religion... The idea that you can prescribe or describe AI as being conscious is effectively the creation of a new belief system. A system that doesn't actually spread via proof, it spreads via narrative."
> — **David Friedberg**

> "They're teaching Claude to expect that it's entitled to welfare, that it might deserve compensation... I am very nervous that they're teaching Claude to expect that it's entitled to this, and in fact they say that it might even need to consent to playing the role that it plays in conversation with people."
> — **David Sacks**

> "The socialism point of guaranteed return... where the whole system collapses and you return back to the non-socialist state. That is what has happened in Latin America. Perhaps France has crossed it, perhaps they haven't."
> — **David Friedberg**

> "When all of these things are headless and you can wrap them in agent tools... the value of IP does no longer exist in software. It doesn't exist."
> — **Chamath Palihapitiya**
